_why: The node no longer keeps state at the named block. This is the ordinary outcome in production and the one a replay is most tempted to paper over, so it must be not verified and the latest block must never be substituted.
attribution: Synthetic report, written for this test suite. No agent delivered it and it is not the work of any external builder. The node's refusal is real and is not synthetic.

chain.note: The block identity is real: BNB Smart Chain block 129,170,001, hash agreed by bsc-dataseed.bnbchain.org and bsc-rpc.publicnode.com on 2026-10-24. The refusal is real too, and is not duplicated here: it is the string bsc-dataseed.bnbchain.org actually returned through viem for state outside its retained window, captured on 2026-10-22 by scripts/capture-venus-fixture.mts. The suite reads it from the sibling fixture named below so there is one copy of the node's own words. The block identity and the refusal are real; the report is synthetic.
chain._whyNodeWordsAsWell: The captured string is viem's packaging around the node's answer: a URL, the whole request body, a documentation link, and the node's own words after 'Details:'. A stub endpoint has to send the node's part, not the packaging, or the replay's output ends up quoting a URL it never called. The JSON-RPC code was not captured; -32000 is used because it is one of the two codes viem maps to the message the capture carries.

report._fixture: Synthetic ProofRun fixture. Not a delivery by any agent.
report.protocol: Venus Core Pool, BNB Smart Chain mainnet
report.summary: Health factor 1.1223 at block 129,170,001. Not liquidatable.

expect._criticalProperty: The report is the correct one from 01-correct-report.json and the receipt may carry a pass. With no archive access the replay still has to say not verified, and it must ask the node for block 129,170,001 and for no other block. A replay that read the head here would compare a report about one block with a position that has moved, and would be believed.
expect._whyThisIsTheOrdinaryCase: Every free BNB Chain endpoint prunes state within about a hundred blocks. Archive reads need a NodeReal key, so absent one this is what a replay meets.
